A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same intersection-regression and proposal-grouping research, despite the changed title. Their text, equations, tables and figures are readable. v1 ends with references and has no appendix; v2 includes readable Appendices A.1–A.6.

before.justification: v1 reports original COCO and PASCAL VOC detection results, COCO instance segmentation results, ablations and a classification-oracle experiment.

after.justification: v2 retains original detection and segmentation results and reports additional detector comparisons, diagnostic experiments and appendix ablations.

M1.justification: The intersection-regression, grouping/union and refinement pipeline is retained. v2 adds a Deformable DETR adaptation using four ground-truth quadrants and IoU-based query assignment, and evaluates alternative regression losses. Its fuller YOLO assignment description does not establish that the previously evaluated YOLO procedure changed.

E1.justification: Both versions cover object detection on COCO 2017 and PASCAL VOC 2007/2012, and instance segmentation on COCO. Additional detector configurations and analyses remain within this coverage. Moving VOC results to Appendix A.1 does not introduce a new dataset or task.

E2.justification: v2 adds Cascade R-CNN and Deformable DETR comparisons on COCO. Its VOC comparison adds Mask R-CNN, Cascade R-CNN, YOLOv3 and Deformable DETR to the earlier Faster R-CNN comparison. Cluster-NMS, Soft-NMS and box voting are also newly evaluated in corresponding comparisons, rather than merely cited.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce Deformable DETR training for 50 epochs with AdamW, classification accuracy, localization mIoU and LRP metrics, test-time flips and scaling, grouping-threshold sweeps and additional-head controls. The reported VOC configurations also change. Dataset splits remain unchanged; omitted earlier hyperparameters do not establish changes to the underlying training.

E4.justification: v2 adds proposal-quality robustness, loss and NMS compatibility, localization/classification diagnostics, LRP error decomposition, test-time augmentation, second-regression and classification-head controls, and grouping-threshold sensitivity. The earlier loss, group-size and oracle analyses are retained, while the full-object versus intersection-regression comparison is revised in Appendix A.4.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The additional results retain the earlier point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Shared COCO detection and segmentation table values are unchanged. v2 adds Cascade R-CNN results of 42.5 versus 43.1 mAP and Deformable DETR results of 44.3 versus 44.8, plus extensive diagnostic and VOC results. COCO recall columns, VOC R-101/AP60/AP80 entries and the oracle metric breakdown disappear. The full-object/grouping comparison becomes 35.8 versus 38.1 mAP in v2 Table 12, versus 39.6 versus 40.3 in v1 Table 1; matching conditions are insufficiently established to infer a performance decline.

T1.justification: v2 explicitly defines the combined objective L_total = L_intersection + lambda L_refinement, with lambda = 0.5; v1 presents the component losses separately. The underlying intersection and refinement equations remain equivalent, and neither version adds theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution and broad detector-compatibility claim remain: regress intersections and combine proposals to improve localization and segmentation. v2 adds robustness to low-quality proposals as an explicit conclusion. Naming the method UoI and adding transformer evidence do not themselves broaden v1's already general compatibility claim.

C2.justification: v2 attributes improvements specifically to localization, explains complementary roles for the two regression stages and degradation from excessive proposals, and acknowledges large receptive fields when motivating the approach. It adds the single-proposal/small-object limitation and an FCOS adaptation caveat while retaining crowded-scene merging failures. It also introduces substantive interpretations concerning box voting, test-time augmentation and one-to-few label assignment.

D1.justification: v2 adds pseudocode, explicit proposal-grouping and coordinate-union instructions, the loss weight, the five-proposal cap, architecture adaptations, a code-access link and runtime information. Conversely, it omits v1's image sizes, batch sizes, initial learning rates, momentum, weight decay and VOC training schedule. These are substantial documentation changes, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: Beyond the retained architecture/NMS survey, v2 adds regression-loss literature and substantive distinctions from box voting, citing Weighted Boxes Fusion, and one-to-few label assignment. New references also support LRP and Cluster-NMS. These additions expand positioning against relevant alternatives, rather than simply update citation formatting.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled and consistently names the approach Union-over-Intersections. The abstract, introduction, method and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Comparisons now precede ablations, the standalone oracle section becomes an ablation discussion, and VOC results move into a structured appendix.

P2.justification: v2 changes to a single-column layout, replaces the opening illustrations and adds a pseudocode figure. Earlier loss, grouping and oracle plots are combined with a new robustness panel. Tables are expanded or restructured, and qualitative examples are reorganized between the main text and appendix with additional examples.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the evidence for why the method works and where it applies. Localization diagnostics and the second-regression control address important alternative explanations for the gains, while loss, grouping and architecture comparisons support generality. Pseudocode and adaptation details improve inspectability. Lost training details and result breakdowns, and the one-to-few comparison using a different detector architecture, weaken parts of the revision but do not outweigh these substantial validation gains.
